resources.string: Tap Stop on the floating panel to end the session

1. Pick the side you want to analyze.
2. Open a puzzle or bot practice position using 2D pieces.
3. Start Watching and grant overlay/screen sharing.
4. Set board area to match the exact 8×8 board.
5. Check Turn and White/Black below in the panel.
6. The circular arrow reads the current position again. No starting setup is needed.
Drag the square to move. Drag a corner to resize. Match the grid to the exact 8×8 board.

100–300 ms gives quicker, shallower suggestions; more time allows a deeper search. Capture and board confirmation add delay. Turn off the study line to skip its extra search. Search time does not set an Elo rating.

Stockfish 18 supports 1320–3190 on its calibration scale, not your Chess.com rating. Lower strength varies its position-based choices; it does not simulate a human. Uncheck to use full strength. ★ marks the Elo-selected move. Green marks the highest displayed score, which can be a different move.

Choose one to five candidate arrows. The optional line follows the ★ selected move for up to three moves for each side. These are possible replies, not predictions, and the line may be shorter near game end.
Number of candidate arrows, one to five

This is the last captured crop, not a new live image. Check that it contains the complete playable board. An uncertain square means its piece or background was not recognized confidently. The image stays in memory and is not saved or uploaded.
Minimize controls. Drag the logo to move.
Expand OpenCheps controls. Drag to move.
OpenCheps paused. Tap to expand; drag to move.
Capture is running. Analysis pauses while settings are open; changes apply when you return to the board.
Analyzing White. Tap to choose Black.
Analyzing Black. Tap to choose White.

Castling needs a king and rook that have never moved. Confirm these rights only if you know the game history. Blocked paths or check may still prevent castling. Opening a position mid-game leaves its rights unknown until confirmed here. These settings apply to this capture session only.

En passant: choose the square the capturing pawn would land on, only if the opponent’s immediately preceding move was the adjacent pawn’s double step. “-” means none. Targets shown fit the current pieces; Stockfish checks king safety.

Scores the board currently on screen after either side moves. Positive favors the selected color; negative favors the opponent. This mode uses full strength and ignores practice Elo and move choices. It evaluates the position, not the quality of your last move.
Optional text only. Stockfish seeks the shortest forced mate it finds within your think time, against best defense. A short search may miss a faster mate or return a partial line.
In arrow mode, choose the side to analyze. In evaluation-only mode, choose the color favored by a positive score. Turn and board orientation are separate controls in the floating panel.
